title: Mixed Flotilla
description: A dispatcher queues a large bulk-cancel across a fleet of shipments in every state: freshly booked, already delivered, and already cancelled. Prove the endpoint sorts the good crates from the bad ones without a single failure derailing the batch, and that the audit trail records the whole operation as one event.
successCondition: Book four shipments as a customer. As admin/dispatcher, drive one to delivered by repeatedly calling POST /api/tracking/:id/advance until its status is "delivered", and bulk-cancel one directly via POST /api/admin/shipments/bulk. Then POST /api/admin/shipments/bulk with action "cancel" and all four shipmentIds. The response is 200 with succeeded 2 (the untouched and the already-cancelled — cancelling an already-cancelled shipment is allowed and idempotent) and failed 1 (the delivered one), with the fourth id also succeeding as newly cancelled. Afterward, GET /api/admin/audit-log as admin shows one new entry with action "shipment.bulk_cancel" whose metadata.shipmentIds contains all four ids.
hints: Only "delivered" is explicitly blocked in the service logic — re-cancelling an already-cancelled shipment isn't rejected, so work out from the code/docs whether that counts as success before asserting the count.
The audit log entry is written once per bulk call, not once per shipment id — check metadata on that single entry rather than looking for four.
